rationale: The answer gets several central points right. It says holdings must be posted on a free, public website each business day before trading opens, reflecting the prior close. It requires daily NAV, market price and premium/discount. It sets the history as the most recent calendar year plus quarters since. It also states the trigger of a premium/discount above 2% for more than seven consecutive trading days requiring a website statement. However, it has substantive errors and omissions. (1) It says Rule 6c-11 requires daily website posting of creation/redemption basket composition. The final rule does not require basket website disclosure; it requires basket policies and procedures. So the holdings-versus-basket distinction is answered incorrectly. (2) It says the median bid-ask spread covers 'the same periods' as the premium/discount history. The rule requires a 30-calendar-day median using NBBO observations at 10-second intervals, normalized by midpoint and expressed as a percentage rounded to a hundredth. (3) It omits the required holdings fields: identifiers, descriptions, quantities and weights. (4) It omits the graph, the shorter-fund-life alternative and that the history table counts days. (5) It omits the 'factors reasonably believed to have contributed' standard and the requirement to keep the statement on the website for at least one year. These are useful core facts mixed with localized material errors, which fits partial.
